record.paper_title: Open Problems in Computability Theory and Descriptive Set Theory
record.original_question: Assume there exists a counterexample to the hf/hf problem, that is, an hf/hf countable Borel equivalence relation that is not hyperfinite. Would it follow that the set of all hyperfinite equivalence relations is Σ^1_2-complete?

evidence.quote: Problem 39. Suppose there is a counterexample to the hf/hf problem. Is the set of all hyperfinite equivalence relations Σ1_2-complete?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Work in the standard Borel setting. A countable Borel equivalence relation (CBER) on a standard Borel space $X$ is a Borel equivalence relation $E\subseteq X	imes X$ all of whose equivalence classes are countable. Such an $E$ is called hyperfinite if $E= igcup_{n\in\mathbb{N}} F_n$ for an increasing sequence $F_0\subseteq F_1\subseteq\cdots$ of Borel equivalence relations $F_n$ all of whose classes are finite. A CBER $E$ is called hf/hf (hyper-hyperfinite) if $E= igcup_{n\in\mathbb{N}} E_n$ for an increasing sequence of hyperfinite Borel equivalence relations $E_n$.

The "hf/hf problem" asks whether every hf/hf CBER is hyperfinite. A counterexample to the hf/hf problem is an hf/hf CBER that is not hyperfinite.

Fix a standard Borel space $X$ and consider the natural standard Borel coding of CBERs on $X$. Within this coding, view the set
$$\mathrm{HF}(X)=\{E : E\text{ is a hyperfinite CBER on }X\}$$
as a subset of a standard Borel space; it is known to be $\Sigma^1_2$.

Problem. Assume there exists a counterexample to the hf/hf problem. Does it follow that $\mathrm{HF}(X)$ is $\Sigma^1_2$-complete (i.e., every $\Sigma^1_2$ subset of a standard Borel space is Borel reducible to $\mathrm{HF}(X)$)?
artifact.status_search_result: A 2024 preprint titled "Hyper-hyperfiniteness and complexity" (arXiv:2409.16445) establishes exactly this conditional implication: if there is a hyper-hyperfinite CBER that is not hyperfinite, then the set of hyperfinite CBERs is $\Sigma^1_2$-complete. Thus the conditional question appears to be solved (affirmatively).

status_evidence.title: Hyper-hyperfiniteness and complexity
status_evidence.snippet: If there exists a countable Borel equivalence relation which is hyper-hyperfinite but not hyperfinite, then the complexity of hyperfinite countable Borel equivalence relations is Σ^1_2-complete.
status_evidence.claim: Conditional on a counterexample to the hf/hf problem, the set of hyperfinite CBERs is Σ^1_2-complete.
